definition: Eclipse Deeplearning4j is a programming library written in Java for the Java virtual machine (JVM).
details: It is a framework with wide support for deep learning algorithms. Deeplearning4j includes implementations of the restricted Boltzmann machine, deep belief net, deep autoencoder, stacked denoising autoencoder and recursive neural tensor network, word2vec, doc2vec, and GloVe. These algorithms all include distributed parallel versions that integrate with Apache Hadoop and Spark. Deeplearning4j is open-source software released under Apache License 2.0, developed mainly by a machine learning group headquartered in San Francisco. It is supported commercially by the startup Skymind, which bundles DL4J, TensorFlow, Keras and other deep learning libraries in an enterprise distribution called the Skymind Intelligence Layer. Deeplearning4j was contributed to the Eclipse Foundation in October 2017.

explainer.lead: Eclipse Deeplearning4j is an open-source Java framework for building and running deep learning systems on the Java virtual machine. It matters for teams that want neural networks, word embeddings, and distributed training to fit into a JVM-based software stack.

tiers.eli5: Deeplearning4j is like a toolbox for teaching computer programs to find patterns, made especially for people who build with Java. It contains ready-made learning methods, so you do not have to construct every tool yourself. Some of its tools can also share large jobs across computers through Hadoop or Spark.
tiers.practitioner: Use DL4J when deep learning needs to live in a Java or other JVM application, with implementations ranging from deep belief networks and autoencoders to word2vec, doc2vec, and GloVe. Distributed parallel variants integrate with Apache Hadoop and Spark, so large jobs require that surrounding infrastructure rather than simply a Java dependency. Skymind provides commercial support and packages DL4J with TensorFlow, Keras, and other libraries in its Skymind Intelligence Layer distribution.
tiers.paperLevel: Deeplearning4j is an Apache-2.0-licensed JVM software framework, not a single model or training objective. Its implemented methods include restricted Boltzmann machines, deep belief nets, deep and stacked denoising autoencoders, recursive neural tensor networks, word2vec, doc2vec, and GloVe, with distributed parallel versions integrating with Hadoop and Spark. Consequently, no one network architecture, loss function, or performance result characterizes the framework as a whole.

explainer.example: A Java team processing a large document collection could use DL4J's word2vec implementation to learn a numeric vector for each word. Words used in similar contexts can then be represented and compared through those vectors, while the distributed implementation can integrate with Spark or Hadoop for larger jobs.

usedIn.name: Java and JVM applications
usedIn.detail: Adds deep learning algorithms and text-vector methods within a JVM-based software stack.

usedIn.name: Skymind Intelligence Layer
usedIn.detail: Skymind's enterprise distribution bundles DL4J with TensorFlow, Keras, and other deep learning libraries.

usedIn.name: Apache Hadoop
usedIn.detail: Integrates with distributed parallel versions of DL4J's algorithms.

usedIn.name: Apache Spark
usedIn.detail: Provides another integration target for distributed parallel algorithm implementations.

explainer.intuition: DL4J supplies deep learning building blocks inside the Java ecosystem. Instead of implementing every network or embedding method from scratch, a developer can use its algorithms and, when needed, their distributed parallel versions.
howItWorks: Write the application for the Java virtual machine.
Choose a DL4J algorithm, such as an autoencoder, deep belief net, or word2vec.
Apply the implementation to the application's data.
For distributed work, use a parallel version integrated with Apache Hadoop or Spark.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes a broad set of deep learning and text-embedding methods available to JVM-based projects, including options for distributed execution. Its Apache License 2.0 and contribution to the Eclipse Foundation in October 2017 also establish its open-source setting.
misconceptions: DL4J is not one neural network or algorithm; it is a framework containing many implementations.
The Skymind Intelligence Layer is a separate enterprise distribution, not another name for DL4J itself.
